Petitioner
 Versus
 1. The State of Jharkhand
 2. Bibi Sakina Khatoon, wife of Khurshid Alam Md. Khurshid Alam,
 daughter of Late Md. Belal at present residing at her father's house
 village Devanchak, Paharpur P.O. Paharpur P.S. Mehrama District

 For the Petitioner : Mr. Lukesh Kumar, Advocate
 For the Opp.
Parties
: Mr. Pankaj Kumar, Advocate
The learned counsels for the parties are present.

2.  This revision has been filed against the judgment dated 15.09.2006 passed in Criminal Appeal No. 03 of 2006 by learned Sessions Judge, Godda whereby he has dismissed the criminal appeal and confirmed the judgment dated 02.03.2006 passed in GR No. 704 of 2002 by learned Sub-divisional Judicial Magistrate, Godda.
The petitioner has been convicted for offence under Section 498A of Indian Penal Code and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for two years.
3. As per the records the notice was issued in the present case and has been served upon opposite party no. 2 and therefore, the service of notice is accepted as valid.
The learned counsel for the petitioner and the State have argued the matter on merit.
4. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that general and omnibus allegations were levelled against the petitioner-husband and his two family members.
He has submitted that the other two accused have been acquitted by the learned trial court and the petitioner has been convicted for offence under Section 498A.
He submits that the petitioner has been convicted only because he is the husband and therefore, the impugned judgments call for interference.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, arguments of the learned counsel for the petitioner are that there was an allegation of taking away the jewellery and therefore, the petitioner and other co-accused had faced the trial for offence under section 379/498A of Indian Penal Code, but the offence under section 379 was not proved and consequently, the conviction was only under section 498A.

He has submitted that the complainant was examined as PW-2.
6.
Without prejudice to the aforesaid submissions, the learned counsel submits that the FIR was lodged on 14.07.2002 and more than 22 years have elapsed from the date of FIR.

At the initial stage,
on surrender on 30.08.2002, the petitioner was granted bail on the same day and the petitioner has remained in custody during the period from 26.11.2018 to 01.10.2019.

The learned counsel has submitted that much time has elapsed from the date of FIR and therefore, some sympathetic view may be taken and the records reveal that some steps were also taken for settlement between the parties but ultimately, no settlement could be arrived at.

7. The learned counsel for the State has submitted that the case of the petitioner stands on different footing in as much as there was specific allegation made by the PW-2 (wife) against the petitioner that it was the petitioner who had demanded an amount of Rs.10,000/- and so far as the assault etc.
is concerned, the same is general in nature.
He submits that the acquittal of the co-accused will have no bearing in the matter in view of the specific allegation of demand against the husband.

He has also submitted that otherwise also, in view of the fact that there being concurrent findings recorded by the learned courts, there is no scope for re-appreciation of evidence and coming to a different finding.
8. So far as sentence is concerned, the learned counsel has submitted that it is for the Court to take a call.
However, there is no minimum sentence as such prescribed under the statute.

9. After hearing the learned counsels for the parties and considering the facts and circumstances of this case, this Court finds that the opposite party no.2 had initially filed a complaint which was sent to the police for investigation and upon investigation, charge sheet was filed for offence under section 379 and 498A of Indian Penal Code.

Primarily, the allegation was with regard to demand of Rs. 10,000/- and as pointed out by the learned counsel for the State and upon perusal of the records, it is clear that specific allegation of demand was made as against the husband, who is the petitioner before this Court.
So far as the other allegation regarding assault/torture is concerned, the same was omnibus with respect to all the accused persons.

10. This Court finds that the learned trial court has considered the evidences on record and the learned trial court acquitted the petitioner for offence under section 379, but convicted the petitioner for offence under section 498A and acquitted the other co-accused for offence under section 498A as well as section 379 of Indian Penal Code.

The appellate court has also considered the evidences and has recorded that PW 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 have fully supported the prosecution case that the opposite party no.2 was married with the petitioner and they were living happily, but after some time the husband demanded Rs.10,000/- and when she did not fulfil his demand, she was assaulted and tortured and was also not given food and clothes.

Khurshid Alam Md. Khurshid Alam vs The State Of Jharkhand on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/161731698/
2 11

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: . This Court finds that the petitioner's case does not stand on identical footing as that of the other co-accused.

Accordingly, the petitioner's argument that the petitioner has been convicted based on the same set of evidence as the other co-accused and there is no additional circumstance or material to sustain the conviction of the petitioner is contrary of the materials available on record.

Rather there was a specific allegation against the petitioner regarding demand of dowry and therefore, the petitioner has been rightly convicted by the learned trial court and his conviction has been rightly upheld by the learned appellate court.
12. This Court is of the considered view that there is no scope of reappreciation of the materials on record and coming to a different finding in absence of any perversity or material irregularity.
No such perversity or material irregularity has been pointed out by the learned counsel for the petitioner calling for any interference in revisional jurisdiction.
Accordingly, this Court finds no merit with regard to the argument of the petitioner on the point of conviction.
The conviction of the petitioner is accordingly upheld.
13. So far as the point of sentence is concerned, the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner has already been recorded as above.
The petitioner has certainly faced the criminal case for a long time.
14. Accordingly, considering the totality of facts and circumstances of this case, ends of justice would be served, if the sentence of the petitioner is modified to some extent.

The sentence of the petitioner is accordingly modified and is confined to the period already undergone by the petitioner in custody in relation to the present case with a fine of Rs.10,000/- and it is directed that the amount of Rs.25,000/- which has been deposited by the petitioner pursuant to order passed by this Court on 04.04.2024, as well as the fine amount of Rs. 10,000/- be remitted to the opposite party No. 2 as victim compensation (total Rs.10,000/- plus Rs.25,000/-) upon due identification.

15. The Jharkhand State Legal Services Authority is directed to remit the amount of Rs. 25,000/-
deposited by the petitioner pursuant to order passed by this Court on 04.04.2024 to the concerned court.
16.

If the aforesaid amount of fine of Rs.10,000/- is not deposited within a period of two months from the date of communication of this order to the court concerned, the petitioner would be taken into custody and would serve the remaining sentence as awarded by the impugned judgements.
17. This revision is accordingly disposed of with the aforesaid modification of sentence.
18. Pending interlocutory application, if any, stands closed.

19. Let a copy of this order be immediately communicated to the court concerned through FAX.
20.
Let a soft copy of this order be communicated to the learned counsels of the parties and a copy of this order be communicated to the opposite party no.2 through speed post.
